General manager | highlights = * 2× [[List of Super Bowl champions|Super Bowl champion]] ([[Super Bowl XVI|XVI]], [[Super Bowl XIX|XIX]]) * First team [[All-Pro]] ([[1982 All-Pro Team|1982]]) * 2× [[Pro Bowl]] ([[1982 Pro Bowl|1981]], [[1983 Pro Bowl|1982]]) * [[List of NFL annual receptions leaders|NFL receptions leader]] (1982) * [[San Francisco 49ers Hall of Fame]] * [[List of San Francisco 49ers retired numbers|San Francisco 49ers No. 87]] retired * Clemson University Athletics Hall of Fame * [[Bay Area Sports Hall of Fame]] | statlabel1 = [[Reception (gridiron football)|Receptions]] | statvalue1 = 506 | statlabel2 = [[Receiving yards]] | statvalue2 = 6,750 | statlabel3 = [[Touchdown|Receiving touchdowns]] | statvalue3 = 48 | pfr = ClarDw00 | pfrexec = ClarDw0 }} '''Dwight Edward Clark''' (January 8, 1957 – June 4, 2018) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] who played for the [[San Francisco 49ers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1979 {{nowrap|to 1987.{{cite news|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/49ers/article/49er-great-Dwight-Clark-dies-at-61-12967034.php#photo-14867116|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|publisher=[[Hearst Corporation]]|location=[[San Francisco]]|last=Branch|first=Eric|title=49er great Dwight Clark – receiver who made The Catch – dies at 61|date=June 4, 2018|access-date=June 5, 2018}}{{cite magazine|url=https://si.com/nfl/2018/05/03/dwight-clark-als-49ers-reunion-eddie-debartolo|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|publisher=[[Meredith Corporation]]|location=[[New York City]]|last=Ballard|first=Chris|title=The last huddle|date=May 2, 2018|access-date=June 5, 2018}}}} He was a member of San Francisco's first two [[Super Bowl]] championship teams. He caught the winning touchdown pass thrown by quarterback [[Joe Montana]] in the [[NFC Championship Game]] on January 10, 1982, against the [[1981 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]].{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/vault/1982/01/18/540911/off-on-the-wrong-foot|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|publisher=[[Meredith Corporation]]|location=[[New York City]]|last=Zimmerman|first=Paul|title=Off on the wrong foot|date=January 18, 1982|access-date=June 5, 2018|page=18}}{{cite news|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=K09OAAAAIBAJ&pg=3637%2C4075274|work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|publisher=[[Cowles Company]]|location=[[Spokane, Washington]]|agency=Associated Press|title=Clark's catch caps comeback|date=January 11, 1982|access-date=June 5, 2018|page=15}} The play, immortalized as "[[The Catch (American football)|the Catch]]", propelled the 49ers to their first Super Bowl championship. Clark played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]] and was selected by the 49ers in the tenth round of the [[1979 NFL draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nflnation/tag/_/name/dwight-clark|title=NFL Nation|website=[[ESPN.com]]|publisher=[[ESPN Inc.]]|location=United States|date=July 11, 2014 |access-date=March 20, 2017}} He served as the [[General manager (American football)|general manager]] of the 49ers from 1995 to 1998 and in the same capacity with the [[Cleveland Browns]] from 1999 to 2001.

Freeney played as a [[defensive end]] and [[linebacker]] for 16 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), most notably as a member of the [[Indianapolis Colts]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Syracuse Orange football|Syracuse Orange]], earning [[unanimous All-American]] honors. He also played for the [[San Diego Chargers]], [[Arizona Cardinals]], [[Atlanta Falcons]], [[Seattle Seahawks]] and [[Detroit Lions]].

'''Dwayne Carswell''' (born January 18, 1972) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] from 1994 to 2005 for the [[Denver Broncos]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was originally signed as an [[undrafted]] rookie free agent by the Broncos in 1994.<ref name="Crash">{{cite web |url=http://www.thedenverchannel.com/sports/5189415/detail.html |title=Broncos' Carswell Critical Following Multi-Car Crash |work=TheDenverChannel.com |publisher=[[KMGH-TV]] |date=October 27, 2005 |access-date=September 5, 2009}}</ref> He played [[college football]] at [[Liberty University]].

Carswell won two [[Super Bowl ring]]s with the Broncos in [[Super Bowl XXXII|1998]] and [[Super Bowl XXXIII|1999]] and was selected to the [[Pro Bowl]] in [[2002 Pro Bowl|2001]]. His first career reception came on a five-yard pass from [[Pro Football Hall of Fame|Hall of Fame]] [[quarterback]] [[John Elway]]. Carswell received the Ed Block Courage Award, after suffering season-ending internal injuries in October 2005,<ref name="Discharged">{{cite web |url=http://www.thedenverchannel.com/sports/5251647/detail.html |title=Dwayne Carswell Released From Hospital |work=TheDenverChannel.com |publisher=[[KMGH-TV]] |date=November 4, 2005 |access-date=September 5, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120315223000/http://www.thedenverchannel.com/sports/5251647/detail.html |archive-date=March 15, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> in a car crash in [[Aurora, Colorado]].<ref name="Crash" /><ref name="Serious">{{cite web |url=http://www.thedenverchannel.com/sports/5200485/detail.html |title=Carswell Upgraded to Serious Condition |work=TheDenverChannel.com |publisher=[[KMGH-TV]] |date=October 28, 2005 |access-date=September 5, 2009}}</ref><ref name="Better">{{cite web |url=http://www.thedenverchannel.com/sports/5212519/detail.html |title=Carswell Upgraded; Could Be Released From Hospital Soon |work=TheDenverChannel.com |publisher=[[KMGH-TV]] |date=October 31, 2005 |access-date=September 5, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120315223117/http://www.thedenverchannel.com/sports/5212519/detail.html |archive-date=March 15, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Carswell was signed by the [[Orlando Predators]] of the [[Arena Football League (1987–2008)|Arena Football League]] in January [[2007 Orlando Predators season|2007]].<ref name="AFL" /> However, he was waived the next month.<ref name="Predators">{{cite web |url=http://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=13 |title=Orlando Predators Historical Team Transactions |work=ArenaFan.com |access-date=September 5, 2009}}</ref>

'''Dwayne Dupree Rudd''' (born February 3, 1976) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected in the first round of the [[1997 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1997 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1997/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-30 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During his career he played for the [[Minnesota Vikings]], [[Cleveland Browns]] and [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. Rudd was a teammate of [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] [[cornerback]] [[Deshea Townsend]] in both [[High school football|high school]] and [[College football|college]], at [[South Panola School District|South Panola High School]] and the [[University of Alabama]], respectively. [[Derek Pegues]], a South Panola alum and an [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-SEC]] [[defensive back]] for [[Mississippi State University|Mississippi State]], is his cousin.{{citation needed|date=November 2018}}

He won two [[Super Bowls]] with the 49ers while earning four [[Pro Bowl]] selections.

Hicks played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]]. He began his pro career with the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) in 1978. He played seven seasons with San Francisco from 1979 to 1985, and finished his career with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in 1986.

'''Dwight Stone''' (born January 28, 1964) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]], [[wide receiver]], and [[kick returner]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), playing 14 years for the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], [[Carolina Panthers]], and [[New York Jets]]. He was an outstanding special teams gunner and kick returner for eight years with the Steelers. He was timed at sub 4.20 in the 40-yard dash and did 28 reps on the bench press (225 lbs.). Former Steelers coach [[Chuck Noll]] said that Stone had “Beep Beep” speed and was "the fastest player I've ever coached over 40 yards." Stone was selected to the All-Undrafted Steelers Team in May 2021. He played [[college football]] at both [[Middle Tennessee State University]] and [[Marion Military Institute]] as a running back and averaged 7 yards per rush and scored over 40 touchdowns in his college career. He played high school football at Florala High School. In 1999, Stone was selected as the winner of the New York Jets' Marty Lyons Award for Community Service, given to the player who best gives from the heart through charity and community involvement

After retiring from the NFL, Stone became a police officer for the Charlotte Mecklenburg Police Department in Charlotte, North Carolina, where he served as a school resource office, patrol officer, and field force officer for 15 years. In 2007–08, Officer Stone was named the Right Moves for Youth Volunteer of the Year. He retired from the CMPD in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://mmqb.si.com/mmqb/2016/02/03/nfl-oral-history-1995-carolina-panthers|title = Oral history of the 1995 Panthers}}</ref>
